chunks: And I [indeed] remind by the name of Allah
whosoever reaches him this letter of mine when he set out for me,
if I am doing good, let him help me;
and if I am doing wrong, let him try to win me back [to the right].

key_terms.أُذَكِّرُ اللَّهَ: I remind by the name of Allah / I call upon Allah
key_terms.اسْتَعْتَبَنِي: let him try to win me back / reconcile me

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali ask the people of Kufa to do in his letter when he marched to Basra?
ai.summary: This epistle, sent during Imam Ali’s march from Medina to Basra, underscores the principle of *muhasaba* (self-accountability) and the leader's readiness to be corrected by the community, reflecting the Shia ideal of a just ruler who is not above scrutiny. It highlights the reciprocal covenant between the Imam and the people, where their support is contingent upon his adherence to divine justice, a theme central to his governance in Kufa.

en.sayed-ali-raza: In any case, to whomsoever this letter of mine reaches, I appeal to him in the name of Allāh that he should come to me and if I am in the right he should help me; but if I am in the wrong then he should try to get me to the right according to his view.
